checks: The cells, rate variables, common inball, grouping, and actual measures are those of the exact same-batch positive-rate theorem. On {L>0} inverse weights converge locally uniformly and body indicators converge almost everywhere. Radial gauges about a common inball center converge locally uniformly, their a.e. gradients converge by convex subgradient inequalities, and the bounded radial area Jacobian gives unweighted normal-bundle weak convergence. Thus the ordinary exterior logarithm away from the zero set dominates each group there.

For fixed T the continuous tail [ell_j−T]_+ has derivative −1_{L_j<e^(−T)}c_ij/A_ij almost everywhere. A threshold level with positive volume in a constant cell has c_ij=0 and causes no derivative contribution. Continuity makes the intragroup contributions cancel. Uniform bulk log integrability and the accepted intergroup coarea estimate make the errors vanish as T increases.

q_T is continuous at 0, e^(−T) and 1. Uniform parameter convergence and bounded logarithmic mass justify replacing q_T(L_j) by q_T(L) in the exterior weak limit. q_T is exactly one on the zero set, and its ordinary integrable part vanishes as T grows. For each cell inverse limit, levels of positive mass form a countable exceptional set. Uniform convergence and Portmanteau pass the moving indicator at the other levels, then the low positive levels shrink to the empty set off L=0.

The boundary tangential coarea bound controls the entire small-parameter collar on the nonparallel region, so it applies even to the rate-zero residual. The support sign and constant-plane exclusion from the positive-rate proof still apply. Dotting the zeroth flux with the negative unit normal correctly turns c_i into −|c_i| on the right side and gives equality of the two full spatial marginals.

All positive rates in either measure are on L=0. Each U_R for R>0 preserves total spatial mass and has no atom at zero. Subtracting its spatial marginal from the full spatial identity identifies exactly the rate-zero atom, with U_0=δ_0.
